«Je laisse pas passer ça»: le dernier ap: “I won’t let this slide”: Georges-Hervé Awashish’s last call for justice
Georges-Hervé Awashish, âgé de 53 ans, a: Georges-Hervé Awashish, 53, had been admitted to the Chicoutimi hospital because he had several health problems requiring specialized care. From his hospital room, he wanted to tell us about his experience. Two days after the death of Joyce Echaquan, the Atikamekw man from Obedjiwan said he had heard hospital nursing staff make death threats against him.
Dans la nuit du 30 septembre, vers 3 h d: In the night of September 30, around 3 a.m., Georges-Hervé got up to go to the washroom. When he came back to his room on the fourth floor, he heard staff talking in the corridor. “They were talking about Manawan, about Mr. Echaquan, and laughing,” he said. Shaken, Mr. Awashish didn’t say a word in his room, which is close to the nurses’ station.
Il s’assoit dans son fauteuil roulant. «: He sat down in his wheelchair. “After that, I heard one of the nurses say: ‘We’ve got one, we’ve got an Indian here, lying in the room.’ And then another one said: ‘We should inject him with something toxic, and then his problem will be solved, he doesn’t walk the same anymore.’ After that, they started laughing. They were laughing in the corridor,” he told us. “Well, of course I won’t let that slide, threats like that.
Je veux plus que ça arrive à d’autres pa: I don’t want it to happen to other patients anymore. I still have a hard time finding the words. I’m living with a lot of anxiety… It’s really, really disappointing what they said, I find it very disappointing.” – Georges-Hervé Awashish
Quelques heures avant sa mort, le 11 oct: A few hours before his death, on October 11 around 4 a.m., Georges-Hervé wrote to his son, Shawnok, to let him know he had asked for sedatives. “I’m going back to bed, I asked for sedatives. Take care of yourself, OK son… Thank you so much for being there,” he wrote to him on Messenger. “Sleep well, Dad […] I’ll always be there for you.”
Ce fut leur dernier échange.Dans un cour: It was their last exchange. In an email sent to La Converse, the Chicoutimi hospital said it does not comment on the health of its patients and that the findings of an external investigation into the allegations in this case will be presented in a few days. The hospital is also investigating the causes of Mr. Awashish’s death.
« Nous sommes surpris parce qu’il devait: “We’re surprised because he was supposed to be transferred to the Roberval hospital, since his health had improved,” says Mélanie Boivin, director of the Lac-Saint-Jean Native Friendship Centre. The deceased’s sister, Louisette Awashish, spoke with her brother the day before he died.
« Il m’avait dit qu’il devait sortir de: “He had told me he had to get out of that hospital […] He was doing well, he was laughing, and he told me to come visit him Sunday morning,” she says. The family doesn’t want to jump to conclusions and is anxiously awaiting the investigation and autopsy reports. Louisette Awashish wants to see all of her brother’s medical records, from his admission to the hospital until his death.
Georges-Hervé Awashish a été exposé à Ro: Georges-Hervé Awashish lay in repose in Roberval on Monday, October 19. He will then lie in repose in his hometown of Obedjiwan. His funeral will be held on October 22. The family is collecting donations to cover funeral costs.
